target: Number of USGS catalogue earthquakes with magnitude >= 5.0 and epicentre in a 10x10 degree cell during the 7 days [T, T+7d) after the forecast origin T.

features.name: std_13w
features.definition: Population standard deviation of the 13 weekly counts before T.

features.name: neighbor_mean_4w
features.definition: Mean weekly count over [T-28d, T) summed over the up-to-8 adjacent cells (longitude wraps).

features.name: large_4w
features.definition: Number of M>=6.0 events in the region in [T-28d, T) (independent of the threshold).

features.name: weeks_since_last
features.definition: Whole weeks between T and the latest week before T with a qualifying event (0 = last week); 52 means none in the previous 52 weeks.

selection_rule: Lowest validation mean Poisson deviance within each family; gradient boosting is chosen over the GLM only if it is more than 1% better on validation.
dispersion_method: NB2 maximum likelihood on validation predictions
limitations: Counts aggregate a whole 10-degree cell; the forecast says nothing about where in the cell, when in the week, or how large any individual earthquake will be.
Most of the forecast skill comes from persistence of ongoing sequences (recent counts); the model cannot anticipate a sequence that has not started.
Intervals assume a negative-binomial distribution with one dispersion for all regions; coverage is checked on the test period and varies by region.
Catalogue completeness at M4.5 varies by region and over time; counts are compared only within each cell, never across cells.
Live features use the USGS feed at the forecast origin; events posted late lower the most recent count.
